purpose: Frozen reference for the promotion gate. The gate must judge the CODE against fixed targets, not against a baseline re-measured on whatever the corpus happens to contain that day.
why_this_exists: The corpus drifts (memories added, content edited, links rebuilt). A baseline measured in the same run as the candidate therefore moves on its own: on 2026-09-12 the baseline gained exactly one rank step (MRR 0.740196 -> 0.769608) while the corrected routing was byte-identical at MRR 0.754902. That flipped the verdict from keep to revert with no code change. A verdict that reports the corpus instead of the code is not a gate.

source_run.note: the last audited run whose verdict was keep, before the corpus drift

no_answer_false_result_rate.rationale: The corrected routing exists to stop returning results for questions the corpus cannot answer. This target does not depend on the corpus: it is a property of the routing policy. It is the criterion that must not be traded away.

mrr_floor.rationale: A point value is the wrong shape here. MRR moves when the corpus reorders even one question, with no code change: during this session final-06 swapped two ranks because the live database lost one edge (memory_edges rows 138 -> 137), costing exactly one rank step (0.5/17 = 0.029412) and taking the corrected MRR from 0.754902 to 0.72549. A floor one step below the reference would flap on a single reorder. The floor is therefore the reference MINUS N rank steps, with N=2, so it measures 'the routing did not collapse' rather than 'the corpus held still'.

recall_at_5_floor.rationale: The baseline's recall at freeze minus the same 0.05 tolerance the earlier gate allowed, so a small recall trade for eliminating false results stays acceptable.
